newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks bounce back as Dow rebounds.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks bounce back as Dow rebounds.

text.p: SPI futures 2630.0 +28 US 30yr cl 6.52 -0.02
10yrbond futs 93.425 +0.040 Gold NY 321.35 Lon fix 322.60
*Stocks rebound after Monday's Wall St-inspired sell-off as Dow bounces back, locals await results. Volume 20.73 million, value A$48.78 million, 428 stocks traded, 109 steady, 275 up, 44 down.
The Australian share market headed higher at the open on Tuesday with a rebound on Wall Street providing enough motivation to bring ensure a firmer tone.
However, much of the local focus was on profits with newspaper publishers John Fairfax and Australian Provincial Newspapers, serum maker CSL and Capral Aluminium all due to report later today.

By 10.10 a.m. (0010 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 23.4 points higher at 2,641.9, while September share price index futures were 28 points higher at 2,630, an 11.9 point discount to the underlying market.

"New York was up last night and we have bounced back a bit even if the volumes are nothing to speak of so far," said a Sydney-based dealer, adding that near term business was likely to be a little choppy.
"We are in the thick of the results at the moment so that may push things around a little."
In broader terms, the meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve later today will be watched with interest although policy is expected to remain unchanged.
Among the leaders Rio Tinto and WMC failed to share in the bounce as weaker metals prices pressured miners.
Rio shares lost eight cents to A$20.90, while WMC edged a cent lower to A$7.27.
Fellow miner and bellwether BHP found support in its role as market leader, adding 17.2 cents to A$17.28.
Among industrials, media giant News Corp was steady at A$5.92 ahead of its full year results due early on Wednesday in Sydney time.
Bendigo Bank shares were steady at A$4.50 after a 13 percent lower year net profit of A$11.04 million.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of over six to one, while about 25 percent of stocks traded remained steady.

In other local markets, the Australian dollar had dropped half a cent in overnight trade to its lowest level in one week and was testing the key support level of US$0.7380 in early local trade. By 10.45 a.m. (0045 GMT) the Australian dollar was trading at US$0.7382/87, down from US$0.7423/28 late on Monday.
Australian bond yields were down slightly in the wake of a firm U.S. Treasury market on Monday, but interest was extremely light ahead of the Reserve Bank quarterly bulletin at 3.00 p.m. (0500 GMT).
By 10.45 a.m. (0045 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 6.62 percent, down from Monday's 6.67 percent.
